subject: Exception Request: Nonlinear Staircase Discount & License Swap for Neptune Labs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ari Khan <ari.khan@neptunelabs.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exception Request: Nonlinear Staircase Discount & License Swap for Neptune Labs

Team —

Quick summary: Neptune Labs (prospect -> likely pilot, vertical: medical devices) is asking for a nonstandard pricing structure that mixes a stepped (nonlinear) ramp discount with a one-time license swap (move two dedicated seats into a higher token tier to reduce per-token cost). They want an answer before EOD Friday so they can include terms in their board materials.

Why this is different: the effective blended ASP falls below our standard guardrails for a 12-month pilot due to the license swap (it reduces monthly list revenue but increases committed token volume expectation). Procurement is sensitive to early-stage reimbursement schedules — they argue the license swap is cheaper operationally than committing to additional seats.

Request: I need VP/CFO signoff to approve an exception to the pricing guardrails and to commit to a 10% deeper first-quarter ramp discount (applied only to months 1–3) plus the license-swap concession. We propose:
- Q1 ramp discount: additional 10% off listed pilot rate (months 1–3 only)
- License swap credit: convert two Standard seats to High-Throughput seats for pilot at a one-time credit of $12k
- Safeguard: automatic step-up to standard pricing after month 3 unless usage hits agreed thresholds in MAP

Attachments: pricing breakdown, MAP, and the short exception memo (summarized in the attached doc).

Why I recommend approval:
- High strategic upside: Neptune is a referenceable prospect in med-dev with channel connections (expected ARR > $750k in 18 months if pilot converts)
- Risk mitigation: we include explicit usage gates and an auto-revert clause; finance downside is capped to the one-time credit + Q1 discount
- Time sensitivity: board procurement cycle (they asked for the commitment to show to the CFO).

Can you review and advise whether we have buy-in to move to an exec approval memo? If yes, I will route the doc to Legal and request DocuSign placeholders.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Exception Request: Nonlinear Staircase Discount & License Swap for Neptune Labs

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask. A few things I need before I can sign off or escalate to CFO:
1) Clear 12-month ARR projection with sensitivity (convert vs. churn scenarios). Please attach a 3-line P&L impact: best/likely/worst for finance.
2) Confirm whether this affects any existing guardrails for our Dedicated seat inventory (do we need to reserve capacity?)
3) Spell out the clawback/auto-revert language we plan to use in the contract (I want the legal team looped early).
4) Is there precedent in the last 12 months for a swap of that size? If yes, include comparable deals and outcomes.

Assuming the downside cash exposure is limited and Legal approves the revert language, I am open to preparing a short memo for CFO review. If you can get me the P&L & precedent by EOD Thursday I will shepherd it to finance.

-Markus
VP, Finance Operations
markus.klein@redwood.com

Folks —

Attached: npl_pricing_breakdown_v3.xlsx and redwood_exception_memo.docx. Key excerpts pasted below for quick review.

P&L scenarios (12 months) — condensed:
- Best: Pilot converts month 4 -> ARR ramp to $820k; net revenue after concessions recovers to +15% over list by month 9
- Likely: Pilot converts month 6 -> ARR 420k; net revenue flat at month 12 (breakeven with marketing credit amortized)
- Worst: Pilot fails -> one-time exposure = $12k license credit + $45k discount revenue foregone over Q1 (~$57k total)

Capacity impact: We have reserve headroom on Dedicated pool for the pilot horizon; no capacity carve required.

Clawback language (proposed): "If Neptune Labs does not reach mutually agreed usage thresholds by the end of month 3, Redwood will issue an invoice adjustment to reconcile the license swap credit and apply standard list pricing retroactively to month 4 onward; Neptune will become liable for the delta over the original credited amount." Legal draft attached for review.

Precedent: Similar (smaller) license-swap approved for HelixBio in Q3 2025; spreadsheet includes outcome notes (pilot converted).

Ask: Markus — can you prepare the two-paragraph exec memo for CFO (I can help with the first draft language) if you are comfortable? We need a sign-off path by Friday COB.

Jordan

Attachments referenced:
- npl_pricing_breakdown_v3.xlsx (contains the P&L scenarios and seat math)
